cases.answer: Natural keyboard focus follows DOM order and focusable native controls. Positive tabindex jumps ahead into a separate numbered order. Visual order stays where it was. cases.answer: A stale element points to a node from the old dome after a rerender or navigation replaced it. Wait for the current page condition and locate the element again using its locator, then retry the action within a bound. Reusing the old reference keeps targeting the detached node.
cases.notes: Dome is an obvious DOM transcription substitution. Correct stale-reference mechanism and recovery, no penalty for spelling.

cases.answer: A DOM replacement can detach the node held by the element reference. Locate the current element again rather than reusing that reference. Also, a sufficiently long implicit wait repairs any detached reference permanently because time reattaches the same object.
cases.notes: Meaningful correct cause and recovery mixed with explicitly false wait/reattachment claim. Retain true knowledge; mixed/false reasoning must not be fully MET.
